title: Working alongside product, design and QA without being surprised at the end

videos.script: Ana finishes the gift card feature. It passes review, the checks are green, and it works. Then comes the sprint review. {{finished}} Marta, who looks after the product, says gift cards were meant to be used only in the shop, never online. Paulo, the designer, points out that his drawings had a different screen for the balance. And Diego, who tests, has already found that the balance can go below zero. {{surprises}} Three surprises, all at the end, all about things other people knew and Ana did not. Nobody did anything wrong. They just met too late. {{late}} This last lesson is about the people you will work beside who do not write code: product, design and QA. What each of them does, what they need from you, and what you need from them. {{roles}} You will see why a relay, where each person finishes and hands over, turns small misunderstandings into big surprises. {{relay}} And you will learn a handful of habits that bring the surprises forward, to the week they are cheap: showing work early, asking about what happens when things go wrong, and saying how to test what you built. {{habits}} Git keeps the history of the code. These habits are what keep the history short on surprises. {{title}}
